pro_course_detail.description:

I will help you guide the conversation in the direction that you find the most interesting, no matter what that direction is.

Before your first text analysis lesson I will share with you a google doc containing links to pages with texts to choose from. However, you can of course choose a text from a source that is not provided by the links in the doc.

For each 30 minutes of lesson time booked I will spend at least 30 minutes reading the text and writing questions relating to it. It would be great if you sent me the text you have chosen at least 24 hours before the lesson. If you do not choose a text before the start of the lesson, or if you send me your choice too late for me to prepare, the lesson price will be changed to that of a conversation lesson.

Reading articles on a wide variety of topics — everything from technology and culture to science, travel, and social trends — is an excellent way to build a deeper, more versatile command of the language. The aim is to introduce you to the kind of English that people use every day in discussions, both formal and informal.

Each lesson will focus on reading an interesting article, which might explore the latest developments in AI one lesson, delve into historical events the next, or read about cultural traditions from around the world. This variety keeps things fresh and ensures you’re exposed to different tones, styles, and vocabulary, helping you build a broad linguistic toolkit.

These readings will introduce you to practical, real-world English — including idioms, phrasal verbs, and expressions that don’t always appear in standard learning materials but are common in everyday conversations. You’ll also learn how vocabulary shifts depending on the context, whether you’re reading a formal piece or something more casual. Reading aloud specifically improves pronunciation, intonation, and rhythm — English has a unique melody, essential for sounding natural and clear when speaking. 

What makes this knowledge stick is conversation. Discussing what you’ve read brings the language to life, gives you the chance to practice new vocabulary, sharpen your comprehension, and improve your fluency in a relaxed, enjoyable way. Talking about different topics also encourages critical thinking and helps you become more comfortable expressing opinions and ideas in English.

With this combination of reading and conversation you’ll build confidence in speaking naturally, understanding nuance, and keeping up with discussions in real-world situations. Best of all, it’s a method that’s both practical and enjoyable, allowing you to learn  while exploring fascinating ideas and topics.

pro_course_detail.title: British Culture: What Makes The Brits Tick. A Journey Through British Culture
pro_course_detail.description:
Welcome to "Discovering British Culture," a 16-lesson journey into the heart of what makes Britain unique.
Improving your English goes beyond memorising words and rules, it's about understanding how the language works in real-life situations.  In this course, you’ll refine and elevate your English by immersing yourself in the rich tapestry of British culture.
Each lesson is designed to deepen your understanding of English by exposing you to authentic contexts, from everyday conversations to historical influences and modern-day practices. As you learn about British customs, humour, and social norms, you'll encounter the language as it's naturally used, which will not only expand your vocabulary and improve your listening skills but also make your spoken and written English more accurate, expressive, and confident. Through interactive activities and discussions, you’ll practice thinking and communicating in English, allowing you to develop a stronger, more practical command of the language.
From centuries-old traditions to the fast-paced changes of modern society, this course will guide you through the diverse aspects of British life. You’ll explore the customs, history, and social norms that shape the everyday experiences of people in the UK.
Each lesson is designed to be engaging and interactive, giving you the opportunity to not only learn about British culture but also to discuss how it compares to your own. We’ll cover everything from the quintessential British love of tea to the intricacies of the class system, from the impact of the British Empire to the modern multicultural society that Britain is today.
By the end of the course, you’ll not only have a broad knowledge of British culture but also be more confident in your ability to discuss it in English
For the course syllabus or more information please contact me

pro_course_detail.title: Advanced English Through Current Affairs
pro_course_detail.description:
Reading aloud, combined with conversation, is a highly effective and enjoyable way to improve your English in a well-rounded way. It helps develop vocabulary, grammar, pronunciation, comprehension, and fluency, all while engaging with interesting, thought-provoking material. By exploring current affairs and a wide range of topics, you’ll not only improve your language skills but also stay informed about what’s happening in the world — using language as it’s spoken today.

Reading exposes you to new words and expressions in context, helping you understand how vocabulary is used naturally. Current events articles, for example, introduce useful terms from business, politics, and everyday life, giving you the language people use in real conversations. You’ll also encounter idioms and phrases that make your English sound more natural — the kinds of expressions that aren’t easily picked up from textbooks.

Speaking about what you’ve read takes things further. Conversations turn passive knowledge into active use. Discussing topics sharpens fluency and boosts confidence in expressing ideas without overthinking. It also improves your listening skills and helps you understand informal, fast-paced English better. Plus, conversation gives you a chance to clarify anything you didn’t fully grasp while reading.

Reading aloud specifically improves pronunciation, intonation, and rhythm — essential for sounding natural and clear when speaking and becoming comfortable with the unique English melody. Over time, your speech will become more fluid and confident, and you’ll find yourself communicating more effectively.

This method works because it mirrors real-life situations. It’s not about memorising lists of vocabulary or grammar rules — it’s about seeing language in action and practising its use.  Because it’s based on engaging content and conversation, it doesn’t feel like study. Instead, it feels like having a meaningful, enriching discussion that just happens to be in English.

Part 1 focuses on the “Introduction and Interview” part of the test – that’s you talking about yourself

First of all, we'd need to have a chat about why you need to take the IELTS Test.

You'll have 60 seconds to prepare what you're going to say ...
Then, you need to speak for 1 - 2 minutes about the subject on the Cue card.
I won't interrupt you at all during Part 2 of the IELTS Test. You're on your own!

IELTS Writing Test
If you're interested in practising for the IELTS Writing Test, I can explain to you what Part 1 of the IELTS Test involves. We can look at the types of questions in Part 1 of the Academic Writing Test, or the kinds of Letters in Part 1 of the IELTS General Writing Test.  (150+ words)

I hope to see you for a trial lesson soon ...

teacher_info.teaching_style:
I believe strongly in learning through doing, in my lessons we will mainly focus on speaking, listening, and some reading. I agree that grammar is important, but should be learned slowly and only when needed. There is no point overwhelming the beginner with loads of boring grammar drills in tenses that you will never use. 

Instead in my lessons, we will focus on speaking and listening, and slowly incorporate grammar when it's needed, in this way learning grammar and vocabulary will hopefully seem less boring and more natural. However, if you need specific lessons focusing on an aspect of grammar this is something that I am more than comfortable with organizing.

exp_info.description: I worked for 1 year as an English teacher in Tokyo (Japan), where I gained a wide range of skills as I had to adapt to a fast-paced environment. This experience taught me how to engage students of different ages and personalities. I also had many 1-to-1 lessons which taught me how to focus my energy on one student's needs. I taught all levels, from elementary to advanced, and I offered courses ranging from conversational English to Business English.

This experience prepared me for being a self-employed teacher, as I had to organise the students and lessons on my own. I used a website that enabled me to teach immigrants in London face-to-face. I learned how to get to know each new student and figure out what kind of teaching plan they needed from me. I adapted my lessons in a way that would suit each student's interests and language requirements.

I taught English online at the same time as providing private tuition in London. Whales English is a Chinese company for children in China. This experience helped me to learn how to teach English and communicate well through an online teaching service.

This was a volunteering position, nonetheless it was a very enriching experience. It is a charity that helps immigrants and refugees from the Middle East to integrate in British society. Therefore, it taught me how to be more culturally aware and sensitive to students from difficult background. Later, we also moved the lessons online at the start of the pandemic which gave me a substantial experience of teaching adults on Zoom.
